summary:
- Overview: Second Quarter 2023 Segment Commentary focusing on adjusted operational sales, which exclude the net impact of acquisitions/divestitures and translational currency.

summary:
- Overview of Johnson & Johnson’s mission and commitment to global health, access, affordability, and innovation.
- Explanation of non-GAAP financial measures (operational and adjusted sales/earnings metrics), with references to reconciliations and supplementary schedules available on the company’s website (Investors/quarterly results).
- Forward-looking statements disclaimer outlining risks and uncertainties, including macroeconomic factors, competition, R&D and regulatory risks, litigation, supply chain, healthcare policy changes, and matters related to the separation of the Consumer Health business (Kenvue), plus no obligation to update.
- Press and investor relations contacts.
- Supplementary sales data for second quarter and first six months of 2023 versus 2022:
  - Sales by business segment: Consumer Health, Pharmaceutical (including/excluding COVID-19 vaccine), and MedTech, with U.S., International, and Worldwide breakdowns.
  - Sales by geographic area (U.S., Europe, Western Hemisphere ex-U.S., Asia-Pacific/Africa).
  - Reported vs operational growth, with currency impacts highlighted.
- Condensed Consolidated Statement of Earnings for Q2 and year-to-date:
  - Revenue, cost of products sold, gross profit, SG&A, R&D, interest, other income/expense, restructuring, earnings before tax, tax provision, net earnings, diluted EPS, average diluted shares, and effective tax rate.
  - Adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings before tax, net earnings, diluted EPS, and effective tax rate, with a note on the Kenvue non-controlling interest impact in Other income.
- Detailed reconciliation of non-GAAP adjustments:
  - Litigation-related items, intangible asset amortization, COVID-19 vaccine-related costs, Consumer Health separation costs, restructuring tied to Pharmaceutical R&D prioritization, European Medical Device Regulation (MDR) one-time compliance costs, acquisition/integration/divestiture items, gains/losses on securities, in-process R&D, and tax-related adjustments.
- Adjusted operational sales growth tables for Q2 and six months by segment and region, including the impact of the Abiomed acquisition and other M&A/divestitures.
- Segment-level sales detail:
  - Consumer Health by franchise (OTC; Skin Health/Beauty; Oral Care; Baby Care; Women’s Health; Wound Care/Other) with U.S./International growth and currency effects.
  - Pharmaceutical by therapeutic area and key products (Immunology: Remicade, Simponi, Stelara, Tremfya; Infectious Diseases: COVID-19 vaccine, Edurant, Prezista family; Neuroscience: Concerta, Invega family, Spravato; Oncology: Carvykti, Darzalex, Erleada, Imbruvica, Zytiga; plus “Other” categories), with U.S./International performance and reported/operational/currency changes.

subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10 -Q and other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

In the first and second quarter of 2023, the company completed a prioritization of its research and development (R&D) investment within the Pharmaceutical segment to focus

primarily in infectious diseases and vaccines including the discontinuation of its respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) adult vaccine program, hepatitis and HIV development.  The 
restructuring expenses of $145 million in the quarter ($275 million Q2 YTD) include the termination of partnered and non-partnered program costs and asset impairments.
